comment: Sovereign Router v0.5 starting model set, exactly per spec v0.5.3 'Starting model set' table. No API keys here — provider keys live as mode-600 files in the state dir (keys/<provider>.key). spend_alert_usd is an alert level, never a cap. v0.5.5 (2026-11-07): rescue_eligible removed from premium/gpt-5.5 — the free-first / paid-spillway waterfall in the gateway supersedes the v0.5.3 rescue pin (owner ruling 2026-11-07). v0.5.6 (2026-11-07): SiliconFlow added — siliconflow/glm-5.3 ENABLED in the paid lane at half of Z.ai direct (NON-SENSITIVE ONLY, spillway_sensitive_excluded) and siliconflow/deepseek-v4-pro present but DISABLED; gateway v0.5.6 enforces the per-model sensitive exclusion in every pass. v0.5.7 (2026-11-09): Groq moved to Developer-plan limits/prices (owner top-up; docs-verified); Ollama TPD seed corrected 400k -> 10M (the seed, not Ollama, caused the 2026-11-09 05:11 self-throttle); two Hugging Face probe entries added DISABLED + non-sensitive-only (owner approval 2026-11-09).

models.notes: Spec: quality 2, small prompts only — Groq free tier is 8k tokens/min per model, so the tpm limit makes the router skip it for large (e.g. Hermes) prompts instead of waiting. 2026-11-09: owner moved Groq to the Developer (paid) plan — limits/prices are now the Developer-plan figures from Groq's own docs models page (checked 2026-11-09). Lane stays private-free (owner decision 2026-11-09): the lane marks Groq's no-training data posture; prices are carried so spend accounting is real.

Spec: quality 4, small prompts only (8k tokens/min Groq free limit). 2026-11-09: owner moved Groq to the Developer (paid) plan — limits/prices are now the Developer-plan figures from Groq's own docs models page (checked 2026-11-09). Lane stays private-free (owner decision 2026-11-09): the lane marks Groq's no-training data posture; prices are carried so spend accounting is real.

Spec registry name qwen3.8-27b (v0.3 registry.json spelling); quality 3, small prompts only. 2026-11-09: Qwen3.8-27B is a Preview model on Groq; Developer-plan price $0.80/$4.00 per 1M and 250K TPM / 1K RPM from Groq's docs models page (checked 2026-11-09). 2026-11-09: owner moved Groq to the Developer (paid) plan — limits/prices are now the Developer-plan figures from Groq's own docs models page (checked 2026-11-09). Lane stays private-free (owner decision 2026-11-09): the lane marks Groq's no-training data posture; prices are carried so spend accounting is real.

Spec: private-free only because data_collection=deny is enforced via extra_body on every call. About 1,000 requests/day shared across clients (rpd). Code quality seeded 4 (it is a code model); other classes at the spec's flat 3. 2026-11-04: reasoning disabled via extra_body - direct probes showed this endpoint's hidden reasoning expands to consume ANY budget (512-8192) on most code prompts, returning finish=length with zero content; OpenRouter ignores reasoning.max_tokens and effort caps for it but honours reasoning.enabled=false, after which it answers directly.

Spec: preview model, re-probe weekly. 512k context makes it the long-context free option (long-context quality seeded 4); other classes at the spec's flat 3. 2026-11-11: reasoning disabled via extra_body (same fix as north-mini 2026-11-04) — as the free lane's only 512k-context model it had become the sticky server for the Hermes agent sessions; its hidden reasoning consumed the whole output budget on final answers, returning reasoning-only/empty responses (Hermes 'No reply' incident 2026-11-11, and the morning's malformed-tool-call loops). OpenRouter honours the flag for this model — verified by probe 2026-11-11 (reasoning_len 0, finish=stop, full content). Incident: docs/incidents/2026-11-11-dots-3-reasoning-empty-responses.md.

Spec: $0.09/$0.18 per 1M, 262k configured context, quality '4 to 5' — seeded 5 for infra/code (its proven v0.3.3 canary work) and 4 elsewhere. Cached input billed at 20% ($0.018/1M). Spend alert $10/month, no cap.

Spec: $0.15/$0.60 per 1M, quality 4, spend alert $5/month (no cap). Daily token limit matches the Ollama Cloud plan behaviour observed 2026-10-31 (400k/day exhausted by 17 Hermes turns); rpd/rpm to be set from the plan page at deploy time. 2026-11-09 CORRECTION: the 400k/day figure was a router-side conservative seed, NOT an Ollama limit — the owner's Ollama console shows 50 requests / $0.07 total for Nov 1-9 with gpt-oss:120b under free usage. The seed caused the 05:11 self-throttle during the 2026-11-09 DeepInfra outage. Raised to 10M/day (effectively unseeded); a real Ollama ceiling will now surface as upstream errors + lane_dead alerts instead of a silent self-skip.

SiliconFlow (international, api.siliconflow.com) serving Z.ai's GLM-5.3 — the like-for-like probe's one clear price win (2026-11-07): exactly half of Z.ai direct on every component ($0.70 in / $0.13 cached / $2.20 out vs $1.40 / $0.26 / $4.40). Quality mirrored from zai/glm-5.3 (same model). NON-SENSITIVE ONLY: spillway_sensitive_excluded — SF's data posture graded UNCLEAR (training not contractually prohibited, retention unspecified, no ZDR/DPA), so the gateway never selects this entry for sensitive turns in any pass. Limits are SF's L0 (new-account) ceilings: 1,000 RPM / 40,000 TPM per account and model — a ~45k-token turn exceeds the TPM window and skips to DeepInfra by design; raise the limits as the account tier rises with spend. Prices read from OpenRouter's live SF endpoints and corroborated by two aggregators (SF's own pricing page is JS-rendered); confirm firsthand once the account key lands — checklist in the deploy record. Key file keys/siliconflow.key via the capture page; deployed keyless 2026-11-07 (skipped as provider_key_missing until the key lands).

Premium lane placeholder carried from v0.2.1 production (gpt-5.5 was 82 of the 104 premium requests in the live audit; claude-sonnet-4-6 took the rest and can be added as a second premium entry before Phase 3). PRICING IS A PLACEHOLDER — confirm against the provider price list before Phase 3; the premium monthly alert ($20 proposed) lives on the OpenClaw client policy. Only level 5 or explicit premium, only for clients with premium permission.

Direct DeepSeek (bypasses DeepInfra). Accounting at PEAK rates ($1.32 in / $0.044 cached / $3.96 out); off-peak (most of the MT day) is exactly half ($0.66 / $0.022 / $1.98). Peak windows 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC weekdays. Quality: reasoning 5 (HLE #8, 60.0%); code/infra 5 (V4 family already carries 5/5 in this registry via DeepInfra canary work); chat/long-context 4 (strong but not the fleet's proven classes). Key file keys/deepseek.key via the capture page. v0.5.5 (2026-11-07): the owner replaced the gpt-5.5-only rescue pin with the free-first / paid spillway — as a premium entry this model is reachable in the spillway pass in normal cost order.

Direct Z.ai pay-as-you-go (NOT the GLM Coding Plan, which is tool-restricted). Base path is /api/paas/v4 — /v1 returns 404 on this platform. Quality: reasoning 5 (HLE #6, 62.5%, best of the three newcomers); code 5 (GLM flagship coding line); chat/infra/long-context 4 (1M context, capable, but unproven in this fleet — raise from probe data). Latency seeded high: infra is primarily in China. Key file keys/zai.key via the capture page. v0.5.5 (2026-11-07): the owner replaced the gpt-5.5-only rescue pin with the free-first / paid spillway — as a premium entry this model is reachable in the spillway pass in normal cost order.

SiliconFlow serving DeepSeek V4 Pro — a second host for the premium step (probe 2026-11-07: output $1.50 beats DeepSeek direct off-peak $1.98; cache $0.135 is ~6x DeepSeek direct's off-peak $0.022, so it would win output-heavy turns only). DEPLOYED DISABLED (the Muse Spark pattern): enable only after the with-key checklist settles its price firsthand — SF's own model page suggests $1.50/$3.135 for this model ID vs the probe's $1.00/$1.50 OpenRouter read. NON-SENSITIVE ONLY: spillway_sensitive_excluded, same posture basis as siliconflow/glm-5.3. Limits are SF's L0 ceilings (1,000 RPM / 40,000 TPM). Quality mirrored from deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro (same model).

Meta Model API, STANDARD tier only (contributor tier lets Meta train on traffic; 1.1 has no contributor variant). Quality: reasoning 5 (HLE #7, 62.1%); chat 5 (Meta's flagship assistant model); code/infra/long-context 4. context_tokens 262144 is a SEED — UNVERIFIED, confirm against Meta's docs in the probe battery before enabling. Documented team limits 3,000 RPM / 4M TPM (not enforced in limits until deploy decision). DEPLOYED DISABLED 2026-11-05: the account key verifies (GET /v1/models 200) but chat returns 402 billing_not_configured until Jordan resolves the Meta team billing issue at dev.meta.ai — enable only after billing clears AND the probe battery passes. Key file keys/meta.key via the capture page. v0.5.5 (2026-11-07): the owner replaced the gpt-5.5-only rescue pin with the free-first / paid spillway — as a premium entry this model is reachable in the spillway pass in normal cost order.

Hugging Face Inference Providers route to Cerebras for gpt-oss-120b (provider pinned via the :cerebras suffix, per HF docs). Price from HF's own inference models catalog (read 2026-11-09): $0.35 in / $0.75 out per 1M — a speed premium over Groq direct ($0.15/$0.60); the catalog marks Cerebras fastest for this model (~1,074 tok/s vs Groq ~421). Quality mirrored from groq/gpt-oss-120b (same model). NON-SENSITIVE ONLY (spillway_sensitive_excluded): HF routes to third-party backends whose data posture varies by provider. Deployed DISABLED 2026-11-09 as a probe (owner approval 2026-11-09): enable only after the HF token lands as keys/huggingface.key and the benchmark battery passes. HF billing is pass-through (no markup) via the owner's HF account — a billing pool SEPARATE from the direct provider accounts. PROBE RESULT 2026-11-09 (CORRECTED same day — the first read was wrong): the route WORKS. Small turn 200 (0.16s at provider), tool-call turn 200 with well-formed arguments, 36,477-token turn 200. The morning's 403s were the probe client's fault: HF forwards the caller's User-Agent to the provider, and Cerebras/Groq Cloudflare bans the Python-urllib default UA (error 1010 HTML page naming the provider domain). SDK and httpx UAs pass — the gateway speaks httpx, so it was never affected. Cerebras prices do not appear in HF's usage estimated_cost (provider-dependent) — settle the real rate from HF billing after first serves. ENABLED 2026-11-09 on the owner's order, after fresh verification calls to both HF models passed.

Hugging Face Inference Providers route to DeepSeek V4 Flash — a separately-billed second route to the spillway workhorse (the 2026-11-09 outage: direct DeepInfra credits died at 04:48; this route bills the HF account instead). Backend PINNED to :deepinfra at enable time (2026-11-09): the probes showed auto-routing lands on DeepInfra anyway, and the pin keeps the billed rate deterministic at the seeded parity prices — same iron as the direct account, different billing pool, which is the point of this route. Prices seeded at DeepInfra direct parity (pass-through, unverified). Quality mirrored from deepinfra/deepseek-v4-flash. NON-SENSITIVE ONLY (spillway_sensitive_excluded): HF routes to third-party backends whose data posture varies by provider. Deployed DISABLED 2026-11-09 as a probe (owner approval 2026-11-09): enable only after the HF token lands as keys/huggingface.key and the benchmark battery passes. HF billing is pass-through (no markup) via the owner's HF account — a billing pool SEPARATE from the direct provider accounts. PROBE RESULT 2026-11-09: verified serving through the HF connector (HTTP 200, exact reply, usage estimated_cost $2.52e-06 on a 21-token call — pass-through at DeepInfra parity). ENABLED 2026-11-09 on the owner's order, after fresh verification calls to both HF models passed. Tool-call and big-payload behaviour via HF is proven on the Cerebras entry (same router path); this entry itself was small-turn verified.
